purpose: Verify recovery-session safety under stale, duplicate, reordered, wrapped, corrupted, and dual-restart events, and quantify the signaling cost of stronger packet identity.

restore_tag16_bounded.assumption: No state-mutating packet or ACK remains deliverable for 128 or more subsequent update epochs.

session_identity.collision_model: collision-free symbolic tag during model checking; hash collision probability is outside the bounded model

safety_invariants: An active receiver always has a valid catalog.
An executable action always originates from the receiver's current accepted recovery session.
A cold restart cannot be recovered by activation without a full install.
A stale restore cannot reactivate a newer receiver boot.
A stale or wrong-catalog update cannot replace the current action.
A stale ACK cannot make the sender READY for a different pending update.
Catalog corruption immediately makes the receiver fail-closed.

model_check.reason_for_reduced_serial: Force wrap behavior within bounded exploration while preserving modular ordering logic.

accept_if: No invariant counterexample at confirmation depth under the registered bounded-lifetime assumption.
Legacy and unbounded restore-only counterexamples are retained rather than suppressed.
Full-tag design has no counterexample in the same unbounded event model.
Restore-only tag adds less than 1 bit per scene in every registered cost scenario.
decision_rule.fallback: If restore-only tagging fails bounded checking, retain full_tag16 or stop the stateful protocol extension.

claim_boundary: Bounded model checking is not a proof for arbitrary implementation code or unbounded executions.
A symbolic 16-bit tag does not model hash collision or malicious forgery.
The bounded-lifetime assumption must be enforced by a real maximum packet lifetime and queue flush rule.
No external spectrum data or hardware measurements are used.
